claims.text: the gate ran its own scanners and reported eleven islands where the page reported six, sharing not one member -- and this file printed prose "explaining" the gap with a reason that predicted the gate's number would be the smaller one.
claims.why: Describes historical behavior not present in this code chunk.

claims.text: Generated-at, git revision, branch, whether the tree was dirty, and HOW MANY OF THE FILES THE SCANNER ACTUALLY READ ARE TRACKED BY GIT.
claims.why: Stamp dataclass includes fields generated_at, revision, branch, dirty, untracked_scanned (number of scanned files tracked by git).

claims.text: The revision is read straight out of .git (HEAD, refs, packed-refs) with no subprocess, so it works in a bare checkout and in tests; only the dirty and tracked probes shell out, and both degrade to "unknown" rather than failing.
claims.why: _resolve_ref reads HEAD and refs from filesystem; _git_dir handles linked worktrees. Shelling out is not shown here but mentioned in docstring. Degradation to 'unknown' is present in _resolve_ref and Stamp defaults.

claims.text: A key that is absent from the file is rendered as ABSENT rather than skipped.
claims.why: The rendering logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Every field degrades to a string that says it does not know, because a stamp that raises stops the map from being written at all -- and no map is worse than an honestly-unsure one.
claims.why: Stamp fields default to 'unknown' or -1, and _resolve_ref returns 'unknown' on failure.

claims.text: May this page be read as 'the architecture at revision'? Only when git says the tree is clean AND every module the scanner actually read is tracked.
claims.why: Property returns True only if dirty == 'clean' and untracked_scanned == 0.

claims.text: .git is a directory in a normal checkout and a FILE holding 'gitdir: <path>' inside a linked worktree, which this repo creates on every daedalus improve attempt.
claims.why: Function checks if candidate is_dir or is_file and parses 'gitdir:' line.

observations.what: The module docstring contains extensive historical narrative and design rationale, but no code in this chunk implements the described behavior (e.g., analyse_once, gate comparison).
_resolve_ref only reads loose refs and packed-refs; it does not follow symbolic refs (e.g., HEAD may be a symref to 'refs/heads/main').
The Stamp dataclass uses -1 as sentinel for 'not determined' for dirty_paths and untracked_scanned. This may be confusing if -1 is a valid count.
